correctness.rationale: The proof handles all integers L,m>=2. It bounds per-column path-edge count by 2, forces endpoint clique deletions for every double-selected column, resolves the sole m=t=2 equality boundary using an interior geodesic, and classifies exact equality as one selected path cut across all m columns with every clique edge. Explicit constructions attain the bound; shortest-path enumerations and exact backtracking on ten independent small instances match the theorem, but do not replace infinite proof.

value.rationale: Complete exact optimization and classification in the natural infinite, two-parameter family P_L Cartesian K_m. Every maximum configuration has all clique edges and exactly one whole path cut, with precisely L-1 labeled optimizers, a structural rigidity statement not an arbitrary finite slice. It complements the founding Cartesian grid study without being a routine substitution because clique edges create nonbipartite triangles and force new boundary deletions.
